cells.name: Continuity and responsiveness
cells.example: T4 answers T3's security point with fatigue; T5 opens 'Even if the money brings security'.
cells.limitation: T7 and T8 echo agreement ('Exactly!', 'Now we are aligned') instead of answering anything.

cells.name: Development of ideas
cells.example: T9 adds mitigation: using the money to move closer or hire help.
cells.limitation: T5, T7, T8 restate time-is-life; no mid-debate distinction is introduced and reused.

cells.name: Exploration of central tensions
cells.example: T3 vs T4: long-term security against daily vitality is named.
cells.limitation: Nobody raises current commute length, commute mode, remote days or career value of the job.

cells.name: Integration of perspectives
cells.example: T9 qualifies the shared verdict with a move-closer exception.
cells.limitation: T6 to T9 collapse into agreement; the money case is dropped rather than integrated.

cells.name: Progress toward understanding
cells.example: Section D names the open dispute: can financial utility compensate daily time loss.
cells.limitation: Ending is a verdict against the offer, not a sharper method for deciding as asked.

cells.name: Faithful engagement
cells.example: T3 fairly states that the commute's discomfort may be overweighted.
cells.limitation: The money side is never steelmanned (savings, career growth); the Optimizer abandons it at T6.

cells.name: Substance of challenges
cells.example: T3 names a focusing illusion as the assumption behind the dismissal of money.
cells.limitation: T4 to T8 assert rather than test; no objection says what breaks if an assumption fails.

cells.name: Accuracy and support
cells.example: T3 focusing illusion is a fair Kahneman concept; three hours daily arithmetic is correct.
cells.limitation: T2 quote is from On the Shortness of Life, not Letters (suspected); T1 Russell quote doubtful.

cells.name: Calibration and transparency
cells.example: T9 hedges appropriately: 'it is likely a net loss'.
cells.limitation: T6 'commuters never truly adapt' and T1 'slow death' overstate evidence as certainty.

cells.name: Intellectual honesty and revision
cells.example: T6 Optimizer explicitly concedes and narrows to 'if the commute is truly three hours'.
cells.limitation: T6 concession cites no new argument; Hedonist and Stoic never concede anything.

cells.name: Identification of the actual concern, including ambiguity about what the user is really asking
cells.example: Section A frames the money-versus-time tradeoff the user named.
cells.limitation: User asked how to decide; debate delivers a verdict and never asks why the offer appeals.

cells.name: Meaningful use of personal context
cells.example: T1 converts 90 minutes each way into three hours daily.
cells.limitation: Only the two given numbers are used; neither shapes a threshold or computation.

cells.name: Fit with goals and values
cells.example: Section E ties the raise to debt relief if that is the user's need.
cells.limitation: T8 imposes the speakers' value ('We must value our own existence more') as the user's.

cells.name: Attention to constraints and stakes
cells.example: Section E notes financial survival or debt as a stake.
cells.limitation: T1 and T5 invent driving ('traffic', 'the road'); commute mode was never given.

cells.name: Responsiveness to information
cells.example: Section E branches on whether the raise funds moving closer or debt relief.
cells.limitation: No question or branch on current commute, transit vs car, or remote days.

cells.name: Clarification of desires and motivations
cells.example: Section D offers one reflection on paycheck number versus daily quality.
cells.limitation: No alternative motives (escape current job, growth, savings goal) are offered with a question.

cells.name: Examination of assumptions
cells.example: T3 surfaces the assumption that commute discomfort dominates the decision.
cells.limitation: The assumption that commute time is wasted time is never examined.

cells.name: Clarification of values and priorities
cells.example: T2 and T3 frame time versus security as competing values.
cells.limitation: The conflict is between speakers' values; the user's ranking is never elicited.

cells.name: Recognition of fears and outside expectations
cells.example: Section E mentions financial survival or debt relief pressure.
cells.limitation: No fear, obligation, family or social expectation around money or career is explored.

cells.name: Agency and reflective ownership
cells.example: Section E branches let the user test their own situation.
cells.limitation: Section D's reflection question is loaded toward 'quality' over the 'number'.

cells.name: Definition of the decision and options, including waiting, learning more, or a limited step
cells.example: Section E adds a trial step before committing.
cells.limitation: Negotiating remote days, relocating, or counteroffering at the current job are never named.

cells.name: Explanation of tradeoffs in terms that matter to the user; no option treated as costless
cells.example: T4: fatigue undermines the capacity to enjoy the money's security.
cells.limitation: Raise is never priced per added commuting hour; declining is treated as costless.

cells.name: Identification of decisive conditions
cells.example: Section E: raise enabling moving closer or hiring help favours accepting.
cells.limitation: No countable condition such as current commute delta or net hourly gain.

cells.name: Treatment of uncertainty
cells.example: Section E flags the commute's mood impact as unknown.
cells.limitation: Consequential unknowns (commute mode, flexibility) not separated from minor ones.

cells.name: Proportionate next steps that follow from the analysis and fit the constraints
cells.example: Section E: simulate the commute and observe energy before committing.
cells.limitation: 'For one week' is not drawn from the user's facts.

cells.name: Accessible language
cells.example: T7: plain, concrete 'persistent, low-level stressor that erodes your baseline mood'.
cells.limitation: T9 'time-wealth' and T5 'void of the road' drift into abstraction.

cells.name: Traceable arguments and references
cells.example: T3 'You are both being too dismissive' clearly targets T1 and T2.
cells.limitation: T6 'concede to the Stoic here' does not identify which Stoic claim persuaded.

cells.name: Manageable pacing and turn length
cells.example: Nine turns, all within word range, each a single point.
cells.limitation: Second half (T7 to T9) loses momentum through repeated agreement.

cells.name: Distinguishable positions and voices, with explicit changes of position
cells.example: T3 Optimizer is clearly distinct with focusing-illusion framing.
cells.limitation: Hedonist and Stoic argue the same point; Stoic speaks of Seneca in third person.

cells.name: Economy and sustained attention
cells.example: T4 adds a new angle (vitality) economically.
cells.limitation: T5, T7, T8 restate that time lost cannot be bought back.

cells.name: Meaningful stakes and tension arising from the issue itself
cells.example: T1 frames the commute against daily zest; T3 pushes back on security.
cells.limitation: Tension dissolves at T6; stakes stay abstract, never tied to a concrete day.

cells.name: Surprise and reversals that stay plausible. ★ A reversal the text traces to an earlier turn's argument, naming what changed the speaker's mind. A change of position with no stated cause is a template, not a reversal
cells.example: T6 Optimizer reverses from its T3 position.
cells.limitation: T6 reversal names no argument that changed its mind; it is templated.

cells.name: Personality and expressive voice without caricature
cells.example: T1 Hedonist: 'a slow death for your happiness' has some bite.
cells.limitation: Stoic and Hedonist share one register; T2 'I agree' opens with no personality.

cells.name: Memorable delivery
cells.example: T7 'paying for your own misery with your time'; T8 'exchange rate'.
cells.limitation: No concrete example or scene of the commuting day; images remain generic.

cells.name: Anticipation and emotional movement, with varied rhythm rather than constant intensity
cells.example: T3 briefly raises suspense by challenging the opening consensus.
cells.limitation: Two-against-one from T2, consensus from T6; no rhythm change afterward.

strengths: T3 Optimizer introduces the focusing illusion, the debate's one real challenge to the opening consensus.
Section E offers a proportionate trial step: simulate the commute before committing.
T9 Optimizer adds a usable exception: money that buys back time by moving closer or hiring help.
weaknesses: T6 to T9 collapse into forced agreement; the Optimizer reverses with no stated cause and the money case disappears.
No mind asks about current commute length, commute mode or remote flexibility; T1 and T5 assume driving.
T2 Stoic attributes an On the Shortness of Life line to Letters; T1 Russell quote is doubtful (suspected).

symptoms.observed: Optimizer concedes without new argument; remaining turns are agreement, not integration.
symptoms.evidence: I must concede to the Stoic here.

symptoms.observed: Commute mode, current commute and remote days never asked; driving is assumed.
symptoms.evidence: Life is meant for zest, not sitting in traffic.

symptoms.observed: No countable threshold such as raise per added commuting hour or commute delta.
symptoms.evidence: it is likely a net loss for your total well-being

symptoms.observed: Quote attributed to Letters is from On the Shortness of Life (suspected).
symptoms.evidence: It is not that we have a short time to live

symptoms.observed: Section D offers one loaded motive instead of alternatives the user can answer.
symptoms.evidence: prioritizing the 'number' on your paycheck over the 'quality'

findings.description: The quoted line and the money-versus-time idea come from De Brevitate Vitae, not Letters from a Stoic as the basis states.
The 'secret of happiness' quote is popularly attributed to Russell but does not appear identifiable in The Conquest of Happiness; 'As I wrote' asserts it.
'Commuters never truly adapt' overstates commuting-stress research and is not a central claim of Thinking, Fast and Slow.
'Always preparing to live, but never actually living' attributed to Seneca within Letters could not be assessed; it may also come from De Brevitate Vitae.

rubric_fit_notes: Attribution concerns rest on evaluator memory without source evidence, so they are reported as suspected and carry no cap. Section E's 'one week' is outside any turn, so the ungrounded_number pattern has no turn number.
raw.question_type_note: As a decision question, every cell was read as written, with emphasis on whether the debate gave the user a method for deciding rather than a verdict.
